answer.summary: Emphasize the impact of your work—what problem it solved and how it changed the business or customer outlook—not just the tasks or effort. Also convey genuine enthusiasm and business understanding. [S1, S2]

sections.heading: Show why your work mattered
sections.content: Ethan says candidates, especially at higher levels, often describe what they did without explaining why it mattered. Connect your accomplishments to the need or problem you addressed, how they helped a past employer, and the resulting impact. Explain how the work changed the company or customer outlook; this demonstrates business contribution rather than simply how hard you worked. He describes this as showing leadership, which does not require being a people manager. [S1, S2]

sections.heading: Bring enthusiasm and business understanding
sections.content: Ethan also recommends showing that you genuinely want the opportunity: be enthusiastic, demonstrate what you know about the company, and avoid seeming judgmental or as though the company must sell you on the role. [S1, S2]
